cell_type_context: Human BLT1/LTB4R1-expressing COS-7 and CHO cells; recombinant baculovirus BLT1/G-protein reconstitution; radioligand binding, calcium/IP3, cAMP, GTPgammaS and chemotaxis assays
compartment_context: Extracellular LTB4 engagement of plasma-membrane BLT1; Gi/o-family cytoplasmic coupling; second-messenger and chemotaxis output
injury_context: No SCI transfer inferred; leukocyte and heterologous receptor models only
context_scope: Retain LTB4/BLT1 subtype specificity, pertussis-toxin-sensitive chemotaxis, Gi/o-family coupling and calcium/IP3/cAMP outputs; leave TF and target-gene layers unresolved.
assay_or_perturbation: LTB4 receptor cloning and expression; radioligand binding; ligand-induced calcium and IP3 accumulation; adenylyl-cyclase inhibition; pertussis-toxin-sensitive chemotaxis; recombinant BLT1/G-protein ligand-stimulated GTPgammaS assay
citation_note: Primary BLT1 cloning/functional and BLT1 Gi/o reconstitution studies
evidence_summary: Primary LTB4/BLT1 studies support receptor-specific binding, calcium/IP3 signaling, adenylyl-cyclase inhibition and pertussis-toxin-sensitive chemotaxis. Together these provide a bounded LTB4-BLT1-Gi/o-to-cellular-output route without assigning a terminal TF or target gene.
limitations: The LTB4/BLT1 functional studies and the BLT1 Gi/o reconstitution study are composite evidence from different systems; preserve the recombinant G-alpha-i1/G-alpha-o and heterologous-cell boundaries. Do not infer a single Gi isoform, SCI response or transcriptional endpoint.

cell_type_context: Wild-type, Par1-null and Par2-null mouse endothelial cells for Factor Xa signaling; human PAR2/F2RL1-expressing PAR-null COS-7 cells and Neu7 astroglia for Gq/11-linked receptor signaling
compartment_context: Extracellular proteolytic Factor Xa activation of plasma-membrane PAR2; Gq/11-family cytoplasmic coupling; phosphoinositide and ERK1/2 phosphorylation output
injury_context: No SCI transfer inferred; endothelial, astroglial and heterologous receptor models only
context_scope: Retain Factor Xa/PAR2 endothelial specificity, the dominant PAR2 contribution in the source assay, Gq/11 receptor coupling and phosphoinositide/ERK1/2 readouts; leave TF and target-gene layers unresolved.
assay_or_perturbation: Factor Xa stimulation with Par1/Par2 genetic loss and PAR1 antagonist; phosphoinositide hydrolysis and ERK1/2 phosphorylation; PAR2 co-immunoprecipitation with G-alpha-q/G-alpha-11, inositol-phosphate and calcium assays, Gq/11 inhibition and ERK/RhoA/migration readouts
citation_note: Primary Factor Xa/PAR2 endothelial and PAR2 Gq/11 coupling studies
evidence_summary: Primary Factor Xa studies support PAR2-dependent phosphoinositide hydrolysis and ERK1/2 phosphorylation in endothelial cells, with PAR1 contributing in some contexts. A separate primary PAR2 signaling study supports Gq/11-linked receptor signaling and ERK-associated outputs. Together these provide a bounded Factor Xa-PAR2-Gq/11-to-phosphorylation route without assigning a terminal TF or target gene.
limitations: The Factor Xa endothelial study and the PAR2 Gq/11 study use different species, cell systems and receptor activators; preserve proteolytic/tethered-ligand and agonist-peptide boundaries. PAR1 contributes in some Factor Xa settings, so do not treat PAR2 as the exclusive transducer, and do not infer SCI function or transcriptional output.

These composite records support a bounded CCL5-GPR75-Gq/11-to-cellular-output route while explicitly retaining the ligand mismatch and leaving TF and target gene unresolved.
